newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer to pay higher dividend after results.
newsitem.headline: Bayer to pay higher dividend after results.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG on Tuesday said it planned to raise its 1996 dividend by 13 percent after posting record results.
Bayer, the first of Germany's three chemical giants to report its 1996 results, said the dividend would be raised to 1.70 marks (99 cents), topping analysts' expectations of more modest rise.
The group's pre-tax profit climbed 6.7 percent to 4.46 billion marks while net profit soared 13.5 percent to 2.7 billion marks. Sales climbed by nine percent to 48.6 billion marks.

Although Bayer again set record high profit and sales, shares traded mostly sideways at lower levels as dealers explained results had been anticipated after Bayer's management board chairman Manfred Schneider at the weekend said a new record would be set.
Analysts had expected a slightly stronger pre-tax profit but a smaller rise in sales.
Bayer shares traded down 48 pfennigs at 76.52 marks while the broader DAX index was up 0.76 percent at 3,462.18.
Hoechst, Europe's largest chemicals group will be the next to report its key data this afternoon.
Bayer will offer more details at a news conference scheduled for next Tuesday.
